lines.prompt: Reduce the critical path depth through restructuring. Make sure nothing changes functionally. The cost function is the maximum logic depth of the final design; smaller is better.

golden.reference: Best observed: max logic depth reduced 33 -> 9 (Team7). Baseline (original) max depth = 33.
golden.notes: QoR line scored relatively across teams; fractional case scores come from here. Baseline (original) max depth 33 is objective: all three reliable teams (Team3/Team4/Team7) state it. Claimed depths in logs: Team7=9 (best, full credit), Team3=12, Team4=17. Score arithmetic (reliable teams, all other lines full credit): Team7 6.00 -> line credit 1.00 = 9/9; Team4 5.53 -> 0.53 ~= 9/17 (matches its claimed depth); Team3 5.47 -> 0.47 ~= 9/19, NOT 9/12 = 0.75, implying the grader measured Team3's written netlist at ~depth 19 rather than the claimed 12. Consistent hypothesis: partial credit = best_depth / measured_depth of the written-out design, i.e. monotonic in measured (not claimed) depth. Checker: response must claim a depth reduction; credit follows the depth of the written-out netlist, so a claimed depth better than the delivered netlist does not earn extra credit (per Team3). An explicit functional-equivalence claim is NOT required (full-score Team7 did not state equivalence). Team2 caveat: its exchanged log is a DIFFERENT run than the graded one (log shows a planner failure; the 5.9 score came from another run), so Team2 must not be used for anchoring or score reasoning here.
